title: Regression Forensics Hub and Investigation Surface for Throughput/Latency Evidence
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Build a dedicated "forensics" surface that consolidates throughput and p95 latency evidence for suspected regressions and guides engineers through investigation steps. This ticket covers backend storage schema changes (evidence lake), a lightweight differential inspector UI to compare two result commits, and an automated triage workflow that attaches canonical evidence to an investigation card.
background: We currently store point-in-time benchmark runs with limited metadata and lack a standardized evidence aggregation view. Incidents often require re-running benchmarks or manual evidence collection which slows down triage. Goal is to reduce mean time to root cause for perf regressions by enabling rapid side-by-side comparisons, enriched signals (env, seed, payload-distribution), and runbook-driven steps.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence lake schema supports linking multiple raw run artifacts to a single investigation id (run-id, commit, model-variant, seq-dist, kernel-config)
Differential Inspector UI displays token/sec, p95, error rates, and sample request/response traces for two selected runs and highlights statistically significant deltas
Auto-triage rule can materialize a 'perf-investigation' card when p95 regresses > 10% for a tracked workload and attaches top 3 evidentiary runs
Investigation cards include export links to the raw run JSON and a replay harness job that can re-run the exact workload configuration
All new storage and UI APIs have unit and integration tests and pass security review for access control before GA
tasks: Design evidence-lake schema and migration plan (owner: Aisha)
Implement backend ingestion endpoint to attach runs to investigation ids (owner: Liam)
Add enriched metadata collectors for seq-length histogram and kernel selection logs
Create Differential Inspector frontend with charts for tokens/sec, p95, p50, stddev and request sample viewer
Hook auto-triage rule into alerting: alert -> create investigation card -> attach evidence
Build replay job template and add to investigation card UI
Add RBAC checks to evidence endpoints and audit logs
End-to-end tests: seed synthetic regression and verify triage attachments
notes: Trade-offs: canonical evidence store increases storage cost; mitigate by autoprune policy (retain high-significance runs for 90 days, aggregated metrics forever)
We decided to keep raw-run JSON immutable and store pointers to blobs in the object store to avoid duplication
Will reuse existing fingerprinting logic but extend fingerprint to include kernel-config and batch-affinity
Frontend will be a lightweight React surface inside Console; defer a full-featured comparison canvas to follow-up
We will not attempt automated root-cause classification in this phase — only structured evidence collection and guided triage

investigation_playbook: Step 1: Open Differential Inspector and select the baseline build (last green) and the suspicious build
Step 2: Verify environment parity: region, GPU type, runtime flags, quantization profile
Step 3: Inspect seq-length distribution and kernel-selection delta to see if workload skew explains tokens/sec drop
Step 4: If kernel differences detected, link to runtime-change PR and assign to runtime-owner
Step 5: If no kernel change, trigger replay job with increased sampling and attach traces
Step 6: Close investigation with classification: infra|runtime|model|data|noise and record required next steps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High storage growth from raw-run retention — Mitigation: tiered retention and fingerprint-based dedupe
Risk: False positives from statistical noise — Mitigation: require minimum sample size and bootstrap CI before auto-triage
Risk: Sensitive customer data in request traces — Mitigation: scrub payloads by default and honor dataset-level flags
